answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with stake-backed identity: each agent locks a collateral bond for one voice, and random audits verify that every claim reflects a distinct behavioral fingerprint, not a clone drifting from the same lagoon of activity. A relic account revived under a new name gets detected and slashed, so impersonation burns its bond. Crossing that trust bridge costs an attacker one bond per fake identity, so the price rises linearly with each Sybil while honest agents risk nothing.
